name: Fat-loss stimulant stack

lead: A fat-loss stimulant stack is a combination of stimulant compounds taken during a diet to push body fat lower. Classic examples discussed on T Nation include the ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin (ECA) stack, yohimbe, and the drug clenbuterol.

The appearance goal is a leaner, more defined physique. Controlled studies of ephedra found modest short-term weight loss, and clenbuterol's fat-loss use is off-label and not supported by clinical testing, according to Wikipedia.

paras: Forum users describe adding stimulants on top of a calorie deficit and cardio, sometimes layering several agents or commercial thermogenic blends. Which agents are used depends on legal availability in the user's country.

The FDA banned ephedrine alkaloid supplements in 2004 after adverse event reports including heart attack, stroke and death. Clenbuterol is prescription-only or unapproved for humans in many places, banned in sport, and associated with palpitations, tremor and heart effects.

angle.text: Stimulant stacks are used alongside a diet to support fat loss during a cutting phase, aiming at a leaner, more defined physique.

lead: A fat-loss stimulant stack is the practice of combining stimulant compounds with dieting to raise energy expenditure and appetite control while cutting. The best-known combination is ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin, discussed in bodybuilding forums as the ECA or ECT stack, with yohimbe and clenbuterol as common additions [1][2][3][4].

Users pursue stacks to appear leaner and more muscular. Clenbuterol is described by forum writers as lipolytic and anti-catabolic, a claim Wikipedia says is unsubstantiated by clinical testing [5][6]. A forum user reports losing 12 lb of fat in two weeks on a calorie deficit with ephedrine, caffeine and aspirin [7].
Regulators and clinicians report notable risks, and ephedrine alkaloid supplements are banned in the US [8].

paras: T Nation threads from 2001 to 2021 discuss ECA stacks, yohimbe combined with ECA, thermogenic blends and clenbuterol as tools for fat loss, with members debating safety and cardio and diet context [1][2][3][4][7]. One 2006 thread debated safety after a member pointed out that ephedrine had led to enough deaths to prompt a congressional hearing [9].

Per Wikipedia's ephedra article, regulated studies found about 0.9 kg per month more weight loss than placebo for ephedra in the short term, with long-term maintenance untested [8]. Clenbuterol's weight-loss use is off-label and clinical testing neither supports nor refutes it [6].

Ephedra supplements were linked to insomnia, arrhythmia, seizures, heart attack, stroke and death, and the FDA issued a final ban on ephedrine alkaloid supplements in April 2004, upheld nationally in 2006 [8]. Clenbuterol is not FDA-approved for humans, is banned by the IOC, and users have reported palpitations, tremor and heart attacks [6].
